highlights.title: I told ChatGPT to ‘continue’ — it went too far
highlights.summary: An ambiguous instruction caused the chatbot to send three e-mails from Ying Zhao’s connected account. The incident advanced Zhao’s project, but showed that chatbots need limits.
body: Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

I was trying to rescue a plan for a perspective article after two journals had declined it. My take-away was that my concept was not enough: the project needed evidence. I decided to use an artificial-intelligence tool to help with brainstorming.

I study soil hydrology — how water moves through soils and landscapes, shaping erosion, plant growth and ecological recovery. I wanted to investigate landscape restoration on China’s Loess Plateau, so I asked OpenAI’s ChatGPT chatbot to help me redesign my perspective as a data-driven study.

highlights.title: 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' Author Officially Settles a Raging Debate About the Audiobooks
highlights.summary: The series has become enormously popular, in large part because of its best-selling audiobooks performed by Jeff Hays. But fans often choose not to listen to Dinniman's lengthy books at the speed at which Hays performed them.
body: At what speed do you listen to your Dungeon Crawler Carl audiobooks? This is a major topic of discussion in the fandom for Matt Dinniman’s LitRPG series. The books are about a post-apocalyptic future where an alien corporation has taken over Earth, using up all its resources and killing most the humans. The survivors are forced to participate in a televised reality competition called Dungeon Crawler World: Earth. Among those competitors is a Coast Guard veteran named Carl, who is accompanied by a talking cat named Princess Donut.

At New York Comic Con, Polygon got a chance to sit down with author Dinniman. We asked about the progress of the upcoming Dungeon Crawler Carl live-action series and the future of LitRPG in general, but the most important query we had for him was all about the proper listening speed for DCC audiobooks.
Polygon: Fans have a lot of favorite characters. Would you ever be open to writing a spinoff starring another character?

highlights.title: Autumn is here, and I’ve got five micro-moments of joy to see us through
highlights.summary: For those of us who don’t like the chilly seasons, ‘glimmers’ are the way to go. This year mine are woolly, furry, scaly and crunchy. It finally got cold and dark in my neighbourhood last week.
body: It’s time to find some “glimmers”, which is what we’re calling little fragments of cheer now. “Micro moments of happiness that can flip the script on your day” have gone “pretty mainstream”, Grazia magazine said last month, but if you missed the memo, me too. I was busy spiralling into heatwave-fuelled existential dread when trend forecasters explored the glimmer concept this spring – it’s been a low-glimmer time for me.

Grazia’s glimmers included a perfume actually called Glimmer and gel masks that make you look like a ghoul, but for anyone sinking deep into seasonal affective disorder, sheet masks won’t cut it. So I set myself the challenge of suggesting five glimmers I hope are (almost) universally cheering.
First, unearthing pictures of Lenny Kravitz’s massive scarf. The man wears a full flock of sheep round his neck in winter like it’s nothing – how delightful.
Second, who could fail to be thrilled by bluefin tuna returning to UK waters? They can weigh as much as a grand piano – imagine thousands of scaly Steinways hanging out around Whitby!

highlights.title: Inside the mini factory where GM builds its EV future
highlights.summary: If you're driving through GM's sprawling campus in Warren, Michigan, you'd likely ignore the pair of adjacent, anonymous white buildings tucked away in the upper reaches of the 710-acre space.
body: GM is using AI models and a new mini factory to build and test cheaper EV battery cells in half the time.

Inside those buildings, which total half a million square feet together, is a massive construction project that’s still in progress. Once completed, it will house GM’s new Battery Cell Development Center, where the automaker is working furiously to build new prototype cells with the goal of slashing the cost of its EVs.

GM has to build faster and cheaper to meet its goal of selling affordable EVs in much higher volumes. Those EVs will have to compete not only with longtime sales leader Tesla, but also with the flood of Chinese EVs that, sooner or later, will land in the US. And while EV sales in the US appear to be leveling out, America has a long way to go before it can credibly compete with China, the world’s leading EV market.

highlights.title: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump’s attempt to rename AI
highlights.summary: When President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as " super intelligence," you'd be forgiven for being skeptical that it would catch on.
body: Musk, Benioff, Huang, and now Nadella have all capitulated to Trump’s ‘super intelligence’ rebrand.

That Elon Musk was quick to jump on board, promising to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, isn’t surprising. When, hours after Donald Trump declared that “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!” Marc Benioff announced that Salesforce would rename AIForce to SIForce; it seemed like a quick capitulation, but not entirely out of character.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended the summit where the executive order requiring government agencies to use the term “super intelligence” was announced. He’s also aligned himself with Trump, saying he believes the danger posed by AI is overblown. So it was somewhat predictable that when Nvidia declared that it would “commit” $1 billion to scientific advancement, that included “ super intelligence research.” Of course, Huang has a lot to lose if he gets on Trump’s bad side.

highlights.title: Why Paying "Market Price" for Rare Pokémon Card Sets Somehow Became The New Normal
highlights.summary: Pokémon TCG market prices often exceed MSRP, but they can help collectors avoid scalpers' worst prices, so here's why fans still rely on them.
body: Even for the biggest and most popular games, getting products at MSRP (Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price) should indeed be the norm; nevertheless, for those like the Pokémon TCG, ‘market price’ has become the go-to metric for many collectors for one big reason.
Depending on your perspective as a Pokemon fan, referring to the concept as a gateway to ‘inflated’ or ‘rip-off’ pricing is totally valid.

That said, when actually getting down to the logistics of what it means to get a box of new Pokémon cards at MSRP today, the “market price”, well, market — has been the response to a growing problem with the collectables market as a whole, and is still a legitimate way to enjoy the Pokémon TCG (very much within reason).
To first put it plainly before going into the nitty-gritty, the rise of paying “market price” for Pokemon cards over MSRP ultimately comes down to one classic concept: supply vs. demand.

highlights.title: Tense Presidential Elections, a Focus on Domestic Audiences and Oscars Closer Than Ever: 10 Takeaways From the Rio Film Festival
highlights.summary: Hosting a film festival during historic presidential elections destined to shape an entire country’s future is a hefty ask, but this year’s Rio Film Festival managed to carefully and purposefully thread the lines between focusing on the cinema and the industry of today and not turning a blind eye…
body: Despite the tensions brought up by the elections, there was a latent sense of camaraderie and hope at the festival in the days since the first round at the polls. Several filmmakers have taken up to the stage at the festival to declare their support of Lula, including “Club Kid” director Jordan Firstman, who raised his hand into an “L” sign while introducing the festival’s closing film at the Odeon on Saturday night.

At several of this year’s panels at the festival’s industry sidebar, RioMarket, key executives and producers frequently mentioned the need for audience development in Brazil. The consensus was that the country offers already eager cinephiles, with many young audiences well-versed in international cinema thanks to healthy online communities, but there is still a challenge when it comes to converting those film fans into cinema-goers. In one of the festival’s first industry sessions, an in-conversation event with director Marcelo Gomes and Rodrigo Santoro, festival director Ilda Santiago brought up a burning issue: the still small number of cinema theater screens in Brazil.

highlights.title: The one change that worked: numb with grief, I sat in the dark, surrounded by strangers – and began to heal
highlights.summary: Life had come crashing to a halt when I lost my brother. But in the cinema I found comfort and a strange solidarity. In 2022, my younger brother drowned in an accident. His death reset life as I knew it. I had been offered my first proper job; I didn’t take it.
body: At home, there were now three of us. We orbited separate corners of the house, each needing a different thing for comfort: for my mum, exercise; for my dad, music; for me, escape.

It was a long, grey January, and I was stuck in the mud. My brain had puffed up like an airbag against the full force of grief; my head was fuzzy and foggy, my thoughts were sludge. I was so sensitive to light and sound that it felt as if a layer of my skin had been peeled off. Mostly, though, I just felt nothing.

I was in limbo. In my early 20s, I couldn’t haunt the house indefinitely. At some point, I would need to rejoin the land of the living. But for now, stepping back on to the hamster wheel felt pointless.

Getting out of the house, at least, I could manage. But where to go? I had seen a sign at my local cinema for an under-25s membership, which offered weekday tickets for £5.99. It would be a relief, I thought, to lose myself in a fantastical world for a few hours. So I pulled on my dad’s coat, made a flask of tea and took a blustery walk down the hill to Greenwich.
points: Life had come crashing to a halt when I lost my brother.
But in the cinema I found comfort and a strange solidarity.
In 2022, my younger brother drowned in an accident.
I had been offered my first proper job; I didn’t take it.

body: US law enforcement agents obtained authorization to use a controversial surveillance device capable of intercepting cell phone signals to find and arrest a 21-year-old college student who helped produce journalist Don Lemon’s coverage of an anti-ICE protest, court filings show.

The former student, Jerome Richardson, who has since graduated from Temple University, is among 39 people charged with conspiring to violate worshippers’ civil rights and interfering with religious worship at Cities Church in St. Paul, Minnesota, in January. Protesters said they targeted the church’s January 18 service because one of its pastors, David Easterwood, also led ICE’s St. Paul field office. Those charged include journalists Georgia Fort and Lemon, a former CNN host, who say they were there to cover the demonstration.

highlights.title: Neville and Carra: ‘Stain’ hangs over Man City until financial charges resolved
highlights.summary: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have warned that a ‘stain’ will continue to hang over Manchester City and the Premier League until the club’s financial charges are finally resolved.
body: City's victory at Liverpool on Sunday, which hinged on Ryan Gravenberch's controversial dismissal, took them back to the top of the Premier League.

But the win was inevitably overshadowed after the independent Premier League commission found Manchester City in breach of the Premier League's financial rules - City have denied wrongdoing and have lodged an appeal - with Sky Sports commentator Peter Drury describing the game as "the most peculiar day in Premier League history".

"We're sat here not knowing what it means," reflected Gary Neville. "City supporters will be delighted [with the win], but I don't think they recognise right now the stain, the stigma and the damage this is going to do to them.
"Liverpool fans are singing 'going down', they're shouting 'cheats' and you can't get away from that."

highlights.title: For the second time this year, Steam has set a major new concurrent user record
highlights.summary: There's clearly no stopping Steam's continued growth. Valve's PC digital store and social platform set a new user concurrent record on Sunday, with a staggering 43,505,724 million users (via SteamDB ).
body: Yes, that's over 43 million players online at the same time across the world, both in-game and out. Incidentally, the number of players in-game also went up to more than 14 million, itself a new record.

That is the highest ever number of simultaneous users in Steam's 23-year history. It's also the second time Valve's platform has broken its own record this year, having attracted over 42 million concurrent players in January.

Steam's Autumn Sale recently ended, so it's curious the new record was set shortly afterwards and not during the sale. That said, the last few weeks have seen a number of popular game launches, most notably the worldwide release of free-to-play MMO Aion 2, which peaked at 397,905 concurrent players at launch.

Steam's list of the top ten most played games remains mostly the same outside of that, except for the big jump in Deadlock numbers (262,145 peak concurrent) off the back of a major update. Deadlock is Valve's third-person MOBA-shooter hybrid, which the developer has yet to officially announce.

highlights.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Pumpkin, the rescue cat turned social media star
highlights.summary: Struggling to breathe, so big she could barely walk, Pumpkin practically begged for help when we met. Before long I was taking her home. Pumpkin arrived at our animal shelter in March, after her owner passed away.
body: At 25lb (11.3kg), Pumpkin could barely move. Her legs were bowed from the weight and she walked with a waddle. Examining her wasn’t easy. Her breathing became so laboured that she turned blue.
Speaking to her late owner’s daughter, we were able to piece together that Pumpkin was around five and had likely gained weight after two litters and some well-meaning overfeeding.

As a cat dad of three, if I fostered every animal that piqued my interest I would be out of a home. But Pumpkin had these massive, expressive eyes. She doesn’t miaow so everything is communicated through her alien-like gaze. As she lay on her back on the exam table, she was unable to lift her head. Still, she locked eyes with me as if to say: “Help!”

My husband and I decided to bring Pumpkin home to meet our other cats. Jerry is an enormously loud black cat, Doe is sweet and shy, and Dottie is a hunter who gathers my socks in the night. They quickly realised Pumpkin was not threatening. She was far too slow to bother them, couldn’t jump on the counter to eat their food or climb the spiral stairs in our condo. She mostly sleeps on her cat bed, adjusting to her new diet.

highlights.title: AlterMe Review: Fitness Built Around My DNA
highlights.summary: Six months with AlterMe’s smart ring and a fitness app helped me build better habits, but the genetic insights were less revealing than I’d hoped.
body: When I was asked to review AlterMe’s fitness system that claims to use DNA and biometric data to create a personalized fitness, nutrition, and recovery program, I was intrigued. I’ve used some of the best fitness trackers before, but have never tried a system that combines DNA testing, personalized workouts, nutrition insight, and its own smart wearable all within a single ecosystem.

I’m someone who needs constant fitness motivation to stay on track. Rather than push myself through strenuous weights and cardio, I prefer feel-good Pilates and an ice bath at my local David Lloyd gym. But in an effort to step out of my comfort zone and try something a little more challenging, I decided to give AlterMe a go.

I’ve used numerous fitness apps over the years, such as Bala and Freeletics, but not one that suggests specific fitness workouts based on my DNA testing results. AlterMe combines guidance across exercise, nutrition, sleep, and recovery, going beyond simply reporting on your DNA and biometric data to suggest small, manageable actions to drive behavioral change over time.

highlights.title: Why Games Workshop's Falling Share Price Is All of a Sudden in the News
highlights.summary: Warhammer 40,000 maker Games Workshop has found itself in the news for its falling share price, which has left some wondering what’s going on behind the scenes. Games Workshop is one of the UK's biggest success stories, with its stock rising more than 70% over the past five years.
body: Broadly speaking, there seems to be investor nervousness at Games Workshop’s ability to keep growing in the face of rising manufacturing and logistics costs. Some on the internet will say the recently released 11th edition of flagship tabletop wargame Warhammer 40,000 hasn’t done as well as Games Workshop had hoped, but there is no official data to back this claim up. Indeed, in an update issued mid-September, Games Workshop said that trading to August 30 was “in line with the Board’s expectations for the current financial year.”

However, there is certainly a feeling that Games Workshop may have hit a wall in terms of the popularity of its tabletop games, particularly Warhammer 40,000, which has seen multiple new, pricey miniatures released recently amid claims of over-saturation.

Things ramped up last week with two reports from the financial press about the state of Games Workshop. The first, from the Financial Times, titled ‘Is Warhammer still winning?’ The FT pointed out that while GW’s financials are, broadly speaking, very positive, retail growth per store turned negative for the first time since the pandemic in the second half of its 2026 financial year.
points: Warhammer 40,000 maker Games Workshop has found itself in the news for its falling share price, which has left some wondering what’s going on behind the scenes.
Games Workshop is one of the UK's biggest success stories, with its stock rising more than 70% over the past five years.

highlights.summary: Ken Fero discusses the London-premiering story of young South Asian men who stood trial on terrorism charges for preparing to defend their community from a racist attack, co-directed with one of them.
body: Bradford, near Leeds, is a city in the north of England. During the Industrial Revolution, it was known as THE place for wool manufacturing. Nowadays, it has a reputation for its South Asian food scene, among other things.

Rebellion world-premieres as part of the 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival (LFF) on Oct. 14. “Revolution is the beat that drums through this electrifying story about the landmark case against the Bradford 12,” the festival website notes.

Fero talked to THR about how timely Rebellion feels today amid a renewed rise of far-right politics, why it was a journey of more than 30 years, the importance of involving the community in making the film and why cinema can be a weapon.
Rebellion feels very timely. How long did you work on it, and did you know early on that this would be a historic film that also reflects on our presence?

highlights.title: Virgil van Dijk warns Manchester City players to get used to hostile atmospheres
highlights.summary: Liverpool captain says players heard ‘cheat’ chants. ‘I don’t think Anfield will be the only place’ Virgil van Dijk has suggested Manchester City’s treatment at the hands of the Liverpool crowd on Sunday was a sign of things to come and something their players will have to get used to.
body: City were barracked throughout the game at Anfield, their first since they were found guilty of almost all the charges they faced in relation to breaking the Premier League’s financial rules between 2009 and 2018. An independent commission declared that City had overstated their income by £830.69m and would have been in breach of spending regulations in the Premier League and Europe if they had provided a true picture of their finances.

The Anfield crowd denounced City as cheats in various chants and Van Dijk said it was impossible for the players not to hear them. City were unaffected, running out 3-0 winners after the game turned on the 62nd-minute dismissal of the Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch.

“I think everyone could hear it,” Van Dijk said. “Everyone can share their feelings and I don’t think Anfield will be the only place where it will be the case because fans will have their feelings. But for players I don’t think it is a good idea at this moment in time [to share their feelings].”

highlights.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's lead actor reminds us why AI will always struggle to replicate a human performance
highlights.summary: Will de Renzy-Martin, the actor who plays lead character Coen in the English language version of The Blood of Dawnwalker, has reminded us of the value humans bring to a performance, versus AIs generating voice lines.
body: Speaking in a TikTok teaser for an upcoming episode of the My Perfect Console Podcast, de Renzy-Martin highlighted how the spoken lines themselves are only half - if that - of what an actor brings. "I think the least interesting thing about what I do is the way my voice sounds," de Renzy-Martin said. "That is really all that generative AI is able to replicate.

"It's not replicating my personality and the things that I do when I'm in the room, and the choices that I make, which is all the reasons that a director or a producer would want to work with me. And there might be directors and producers who don't want to do those things [and to use AI], but then they've got to get really good at getting performances out of something - they need to have their own ideas."

The discussion reminded de Renzy-Martin of something he apparently said four or five years ago: "Actors are pretty cheap in the grand scheme of things. And if you end up with an AI that can produce the right noises, you're going to need somebody who can interact with it and get the performance that you want attached to those noises - and they're going to be much more expensive than an actor is."

highlights.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
highlights.summary: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of.
body: It’s like using cloud-based AI tools, but the privacy makes it more appealing.

So as part of my ongoing testing of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, as well as experimenting on other Mac and Windows systems, I’ve installed some local LLMs and I’m beginning to tinker. Here’s how things are going.

I started by installing the open-source Hermes Agent on the Mac Studio. Hermes is a self-hosted AI agent desktop app that works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It’s completely free to use if you stick to local LLMs. Since this M5 Ultra Mac Studio has 256GB of unified memory, I could run just about any model I want. This is how things quickly get overwhelming. There are more models out there than I can count, and some have specialized uses. Generally, models with many billions of parameters are able to do more than smaller ones with only a few billion. And since we don’t have to worry about paying for tokens when running a model locally, I figured I’d go big to start.

It wasn’t long to get up and running with Hermes and Qwen, and even make them controllable via my phone by using a Telegram bot. But then, I was presented with my usual nemesis when it comes to using AI: the text box.
points: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular.
Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of.

highlights.title: Gears of War: E-Day Dev Confirms DDoS Attack
highlights.summary: Gears of War: E-Day suffered a DDoS attack over the weekend, developer The Coalition has said. Players suffered intermittent disconnects and login issues while trying to play the Xbox Series X and S and PC action game, which The Coalition eventually got on top of.
body: “Our teams are continuing to monitor and mitigate this activity. We’ll provide updates if there are any significant changes,” The Coalition said. “Thank you for your patience and understanding.”

There is a great deal of speculation online about the motivation behind hitting Gears with a DDoS attack, with some pointing to a continued online vendetta against the game for apparently being “woke.” E-Day has a “mostly positive” user review rating on Steam. Whatever the reason (there may be no overarching reason behind the DDoS attack at all), E-Day is now up and running.

Last week, Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, reported that E-Day had sold an estimated 230,000 copies in its first week in what was described as a soft start. These unofficial figures, which are not backed by data provided by Microsoft, pointed to Xbox subscription service Game Pass as cannibalizing sales.

Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make.

highlights.title: Pasto Cine Boards ‘Puan’ Helmer María Alché’s ‘I Love You and Today Everything Looks Beautiful’ (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil – Argentina’s Pasto Cine has boarded María Alché’s upcoming “I Love You and Today Everything Looks Beautiful.” The film is produced by leading Brazilian banner Bubbles Project alongside Spain’s Elastica Films, Germany’s Pandora Film, and France’s Maneki Films.
body: Actress, screenwriter, and director Alché wrote and directed “Puan” alongside Benjamín Naishtat (“Glaxo”). The film won the Silver Shell for Actor and Screenplay at the San Sebastián Film Festival, was nominated for the Goya Awards, and was a box office hit in Argentina.

She co-wrote Lucrecia Martel’s “Nuestra tierra” and wrote and directed the feature film “A Family Submerged,” which won the Horizontes Latinos Award in San Sebastián, the Ingmar Bergman Award for Best First Feature at the Goteborg Film Festival, Best Screenplay at the Lima Film Festival, and Best Director at Ficunam.

Alché’s latest is currently in the financing stages and is aiming to shoot in the second half of 2027. Renowned French cinematographer Hélène Louvart (“La Chimera,” “The Lost Daughter”) has also joined the project, as have “Divine Love” editor Livia Serpa and “I’m Still Here” sound director Laura Zimerman. This is the third collaboration between the Argentinian director and Tatiana Leite’s Bubbles Project, and the fourth collaboration between Bubbles and Barbara Francisco’s Pasto Cine.

highlights.title: The Shoe and Skirt Combination Sweeping the Street-Style Scene This Month
highlights.summary: There was one outfit combination that swept the street style scene this fashion month; pencil skirts and pointed pumps. Here are 7 outfits to try.
body: If there is one key takeaway from this fashion month it’s that 2027 is destined to be the year of the skirt. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have asked us all to pause on wearing trousers and dresses for the foreseeable, as the spring/summer 2027 Prada collection featured 63 looks that all centred around a skirt. What Miuccia says always carries weight, and the street style crowd are already responding to her no-trousers directive.

Although the street style galleries feature many different skirt trends, from fall florals to colour-pop midis, if we had to declare one outfit as the uniform of the spring/summer 2027 show circuit it would be a column pencil skirt paired with pointed pumps.

Although you’d be forgiven for thinking there is something rather Apprentice about a suit skirt and court shoes, there is a softness to the styling that stops it being too severe or corporate. Jeanne Damas, for example, wore a pair of black glossy slingbacks with a black tailored skirt, which provided a polished base to her otherwise relaxed weekend staples (she wore a shirt with rolled-up sleeves under a striped jumper and a pair of aviators).
